ingredientsPage.title: The 4 Sacred Ingredients
ingredientsPage.subtitle: Potato, egg, olive oil, and salt form the sacred, unshakeable foundation of authentic Spanish tortilla.
ingredientsPage.sacredSectionSubtitle: Without these four core elements, there is no tortilla. Quality raw ingredients and balance are everything.
ingredientsPage.optionalSectionSubtitle: Traditional additions and personal touches that enrich or vary the recipe across different regions or personal preference.

potatoes.title: The Potato
potatoes.subtitle: Monalisa, Kennebec, or Yukon Gold
potatoes.desc: We seek potatoes with a balanced starch and water ratio. Monalisa or Kennebec are ideal because they turn tender and creamy when poached without completely falling apart.

eggs.title: The Egg
eggs.subtitle: Free-range pasture raised eggs
eggs.desc: The yolk provides creaminess and rich golden color. Room-temperature fresh eggs ensure smooth emulsification without over-whisking.

oil.title: Olive Oil
oil.subtitle: Mild Extra Virgin Olive Oil (Arbequina)
oil.desc: Not merely a lubricant: it is the cooking medium that confits the potatoes. High quality EVOO adds fruity notes without overpowering the natural potato flavor.

salt.title: Salt
salt.subtitle: Fine sea salt
salt.desc: Salt should be added to the beaten eggs, not just the potatoes. Salt solubilizes egg proteins, allowing for a silky smooth setting.

onion.title: The Onion
onion.subtitle: Sweet yellow onion (Optional - The Eternal Debate)
onion.desc: For onion enthusiasts, thinly sliced onion adds natural moisture and caramelized sugars that complement the savory egg.

peppers.title: Bell & Frying Peppers
peppers.subtitle: Green or red peppers (Optional - Country / Paisana Style)
peppers.desc: Fresh sweet or frying peppers that bring garden aromas and color to regional varieties like Basque tortilla paisana. Note: distinct from black pepper.

garlic.title: Garlic
garlic.subtitle: Garlic clove (Optional - Aromatic Infusion)
garlic.desc: A garlic clove gently sizzled in the olive oil before poaching potatoes infuses a subtle savory aroma and countryside depth without overpowering.

blackPepper.title: Black Pepper
blackPepper.subtitle: Freshly cracked black pepper (Optional aromatic touch)
blackPepper.desc: A subtle pinch of freshly cracked black pepper in the beaten eggs adds warmth and enhances the aromatic notes of the olive oil without overwhelming the potato.

techniquesPage.title: Critical Culinary Techniques
techniquesPage.subtitle: From the initial slicing of potatoes to the confident flip in the pan.

step1.title: 1. Slicing & Chipping
step1.desc: Slice potatoes into thin, irregular bites ('chascar'). Breaking the potato releases natural starches that thicken the mixture.

step2.title: 2. Slow Confit (Pochado)
step2.desc: Submerge potatoes in olive oil at medium-low heat (130°C - 140°C / 265°F - 285°F). They must cook slowly until tender, not crisp.

step3.title: 3. The Sacred 5-Minute Rest
step3.desc: Drain warm potatoes and immediately mix with beaten eggs. Let rest for 5 minutes so the potatoes absorb the creamy egg mixture like a sponge.

step4.title: 4. The Confident Flip
step4.desc: Use a flat plate wider than the pan. Place your hand firmly in the center of the plate and flip with one swift, confident motion.

step5.title: 5. Final Sealing
step5.desc: Slide the tortilla back into the hot pan for just 30 to 60 seconds to create a thin golden exterior while keeping the center juicy.

garlic.title: Garlic Infusion (Chef's Secret)
garlic.desc: Infuse a whole, crushed garlic clove in low-temperature olive oil before adding potatoes. Remove before browning to add a subtle, elegant aroma without bitterness.

pepper.title: Freshly Ground Black Pepper Touch
pepper.desc: A gentle pinch of freshly cracked black pepper in the beaten eggs balances the oil's richness, accentuates natural potato/onion sweetness, and elevates aroma.

sciencePage.title: The Science Behind Tortilla
sciencePage.subtitle: Understand molecular transformations, thermal pathogen inactivation, and microbiological safety standards.
sciencePage.chefNoteText: The tortilla is a masterpiece of duality: the rustic warmth of potato and the scientific volatility of egg. To guarantee bactericidal safety, the gold standard always demands **70°C for 2 minutes** to achieve a ≥ 5 log reduction of *S. Enteritidis*.

card1.title: Protein Coagulation
card1.desc: Egg proteins begin coagulating at 62°C. To ensure bactericidal safety, the core standard requires **70°C for 2 minutes** (achieving a $\ge 5 \text{ log}$ reduction of *S. Enteritidis*).

card2.title: Starch Gelatinization
card2.desc: At 60°C - 65°C, potato starch granules absorb water and olive oil, swelling into a soft structural matrix that binds the dish.

card3.title: Thermal Inactivation & Heat
card3.desc: Medium doneness safety threshold reaches **63°C for 20 seconds** (intermediate *Salmonella* reduction for juicy tortillas intended for immediate consumption). The gold bactericidal standard is **70°C for 2 minutes**.

card4.title: Microbiological Risk Management
card4.desc: Runny 'poco cuajada' tortillas feature a pH of 3.8–4.5 and high water activity ($a_w > 0.99$). Unrefrigerated preparations above **8°C** must not exceed **4 hours** at ambient temperature.

sciencePage.safetySectionSub: The three thermal processing levels according to Risk Ranger methodology.
sciencePage.levelPilotDesc: Ambient temperature without thermal control. Bacterial proliferation risk if standing time exceeds **4 hours**.
sciencePage.levelMediumDesc: Thermal processing at **63°C for 20 seconds**. Recommended for juicy tortillas for immediate consumption.
sciencePage.levelSafeDesc: Thermal processing at **70°C for 2 minutes**. Ensures $\ge 5 \text{ log}$ reduction of *S. Enteritidis*.

personasPage.summaryDesc: Each of these individuals provides a unique link to the heritage of the Spanish tortilla. Explore our interactive sections to put their findings and recipes into practice.

historyPage.summaryDesc: A unique culinary journey uniting Spain's living history with the rigor of culinary science. For more details on bacteriology and food safety, visit our Science section.

aboutPage.title: About Tortilla de Patatas
aboutPage.subtitle: A dedicated project to document, share, and perfect Spain's iconic culinary treasure.
aboutPage.storyP1: While popular legend attributes the invention of tortilla to General Tomás de Zumalacárregui in Navarra around 1817 as a cheap, nourishing food for his troops, historical documents trace its origins to Villanueva de la Serena (Extremadura) in 1798.
aboutPage.storyP2: Today, Spanish tortilla transcends borders: it is the staple dish across tapas bars in Spain, enjoyed from morning till night.
aboutPage.missionDesc: tortilladepatatas.org was created to connect food enthusiasts worldwide, document traditional cooking techniques, and offer interactive tools like our ratio builder.
aboutPage.websiteDesc: A fast, multilingual, and accessible website for all lovers of traditional home cooking.
